Step-by-step verification (both proofs of the iff).

PROOF 1 - NECESSARY CONDITION
0001-0002 | Section headers; no mathematical content. OK.
0004 | Hypothesis: alpha : F -> G is a natural transformation. Legitimate assumption for the forward direction.
0006-0007 | Invokes the naturality definition; the squares displayed are the naturality squares specialized to the morphisms (f, id_D) and (id_C, g) of C x D. Both are genuine morphisms of the product category, so this specialization is justified.
0009-0029 | Diagram 1 (top square): F(C,D) -> F(C',D) via F(f,id_D), verticals alpha_{(C,D)}, alpha_{(C',D)}, bottom G(f,id_D) — exactly the naturality square at (f,id_D). Diagram 2 (bottom square): the naturality square at (id_C,g). Correctly drawn, correctly typed. OK.
0031-0032 | "That is" — restatement announcement; the following diagrams are supposed to be the same squares written with the partially-substituted functors. OK.
0034-0039 | Objects relabelled: F(-,D)(C) = F(C,D), F(-,D)(C') = F(C',D), likewise for G. Correct by the definition of substituting the second variable.
0040 | Top arrow F(-,D)(f) = F(f,id_D). Correct.
0041 | TYPO (non-substantive): the bottom arrow of the G-row is labelled F(-,D)(f); it must be G(-,D)(f). The object names on that arrow ('GCD' -> 'GC2D') fix the intended reading, the corresponding line 0016 of the previous diagram has G, and nothing downstream depends on the label. Not a logical failure.
0042-0043 | Verticals alpha(-,D)_C = alpha_{(C,D)} and alpha(-,D)_{C'} = alpha_{(C',D)}, by the definition given in the statement. Correct.
0045-0053 | Second square rewritten with F(C,-), G(C,-): F(C,-)(g) = F(id_C,g), alpha(C,-)_D = alpha_{(C,D)}. Correct.
0055-0057 | Cites the definitions of the substituted functors and of alpha(C,-), alpha(-,D) — precisely the identities used in 0034-0053. Justified.
0059-0061 | Concludes (1) and (2): the families alpha(C,-)_D and alpha(-,D)_C have the right domains/codomains and satisfy the naturality squares just displayed, so each is a natural transformation. Justified.
0062 | qed(lemma) for the forward direction. Justified.

PROOF 1 - SUFFICIENT CONDITION
0064 | Header. OK.
0066-0068 | Hypotheses (1) and (2) assumed. Legitimate.
0070-0071 | Applies the naturality definition to those component transformations. Justified.
0073-0082 | First square: naturality of alpha(-,D) at f: C -> C'. Correct. (Same F/G label typo as 0041 on line 0080; harmless, same reasoning.)
0084-0092 | Second square: naturality of alpha(C',-) at g: D -> D'. Note the proof correctly uses C' (not C) here, which is what is needed for the two squares to be composable. Correct.
0095-0096 | "That is": announces the translation back to the bifunctor notation for a general morphism (f,g) of C x D. OK.
0098-0112 | The two squares pasted along the common edge F(C',D) -> G(C',D): top row F(C,D) -F(f,id_D)-> F(C',D) -F(id_{C'},g)-> F(C',D'), bottom row the G-analogue, verticals alpha at (C,D), (C',D), (C',D'). Each sub-square commutes by 0073-0092 after substituting the definitions cited in 0114-0116, hence the outer rectangle commutes. Justified.
0114-0116 | Justification cites exactly the substitution definitions and the definition of the alpha families. Correct.
0118-0119 | Adds the diagonal composites using bifunctoriality and identities. Justified.
0121-0137 | Same diagram plus arrows F(f,g): F(C,D) -> F(C',D') and G(f,g): G(C,D) -> G(C',D'). These commute with the two-step paths because (f,g) = (id_{C'},g) o (f,id_D) in C x D and F, G are functors, so F(f,g) = F(id_{C'},g) o F(f,id_D) and likewise for G. Justified.
0136-0138 | The diagonal arrows are inserted with the correct sources/targets. Correct.
0140 | Concludes G(f,g) o alpha_{(C,D)} = alpha_{(C',D')} o F(f,g) for arbitrary (f,g), i.e. alpha is natural. This is exactly the outer rectangle of 0121-0137. Justified; qed.

PROOF 2 - NECESSARY CONDITION
0142-0143 | Headers. OK.
0145 | Hypothesis: alpha natural. Legitimate.
0147-0148 | Naturality written equationally: G(f,g) o alpha_{(C,D)} = alpha_{(C',D')} o F(f,g). Correct restatement of the definition.
0150-0151 | (3) obtained by taking g = id_D (a legitimate morphism D -> D), so the target index becomes (C',D). Correct specialization.
0152-0153 | (4) obtained by taking f = id_C. Correct specialization.
0155 | Fixes D and f: C -> C'. OK.
0157-0159 | G(-,D)(f) o alpha(-,D)_C = G(f,id_D) o alpha(-,D)_C by the definition of substituting the second variable. Correct.
0161-0162 | alpha(-,D)_C = alpha_{(C,D)} by the definition in the statement. Correct.
0164-0165 | Rewrites using (3). Correct application; both sides are morphisms F(C,D) -> G(C',D).
0167-0168 | alpha_{(C',D)} = alpha(-,D)_{C'}. Correct.
0170-0171 | F(f,id_D) = F(-,D)(f). Correct. The chain establishes the naturality square for alpha(-,D).
0175-0177 | Concludes (2). Justified by the displayed chain plus correct typing of the components.
0179 | Fixes C and g: D -> D'. OK.
0181 | TYPO (non-substantive): the left-hand side is written G(C,-)(f) where the quantified morphism is g: D -> D'; G(C,-) is a functor D -> E so it cannot be applied to f, and line 0182 already reads G(id_C,g). Clearly a slip for G(C,-)(g); nothing downstream depends on the misprint.
0182-0183 | G(C,-)(g) = G(id_C,g) by substitution of the first variable. Correct.
0185-0186 | alpha(C,-)_D = alpha_{(C,D)}. Correct.
0188-0189 | Rewrites using (4). Correct application.
0191-0192 | alpha_{(C,D')} = alpha(C,-)_{D'}. Correct.
0194-0195 | F(id_C,g) = F(C,-)(g). Correct; naturality square for alpha(C,-) established.
0199-0201 | Concludes (1). Justified.
0203 | "The result follows"; qed(lemma) for the forward direction of Proof 2. Justified.

PROOF 2 - SUFFICIENT CONDITION
0205 | Header. OK.
0207-0209 | Hypotheses (1),(2). Legitimate.
0211-0214 | The two naturality equations for alpha(-,D) and alpha(C,-). Correct instances of the definition.
0216-0217 | "That is": translation to bifunctor notation. OK.
0218 | TYPO (non-substantive): (3) is printed as G(f,id_D) o alpha_{(C,D)} = alpha_{(C',D)} o G(f,id_D); the right-hand composite is not even composable (G(f,id_D) lands in G(C',D) while alpha_{(C',D)} starts at F(C',D)), so the intended and only well-typed reading is ... = alpha_{(C',D)} o F(f,id_D), which is exactly what line 0213 translates to and exactly the form used later at line 0236. A misprint, not a used assumption.
0219 | (4): G(id_C,g) o alpha_{(C,D)} = alpha_{(C,D')} o F(id_C,g). Correct translation of 0214.
0220-0222 | Cites the substitution definitions and the alpha conventions used for the translation. Justified.
0224 | Fixes an arbitrary morphism (f,g) of C x D. OK.
0226-0228 | G(f,g) = G(id_{C'} o f, g o id_D) by the identity-morphism laws. Correct.
0230-0231 | (id_{C'} o f, g o id_D) = (id_{C'},g) o (f,id_D) by componentwise composition in the product category. Correct.
0233-0234 | Functoriality of G splits this into G(id_{C'},g) o G(f,id_D). Correct.
0236-0237 | Applies (3) (in its well-typed form) to replace G(f,id_D) o alpha_{(C,D)} by alpha_{(C',D)} o F(f,id_D). Correct.
0239-0240 | Applies (4) instantiated at the object C' with g: D -> D': G(id_{C'},g) o alpha_{(C',D)} = alpha_{(C',D')} o F(id_{C'},g). Legitimate, since (4) is assumed for every object of C, C' included. Correct.
0242-0243 | Functoriality of F recombines F(id_{C'},g) o F(f,id_D) = F((id_{C'},g) o (f,id_D)). Correct.
0245-0246 | Componentwise composition in the product category. Correct.
0248-0249 | Identity laws give F(f,g). Correct.
0251 | End of chain: G(f,g) o alpha_{(C,D)} = alpha_{(C',D')} o F(f,g) for all (f,g). Correct.
0253 | Concludes alpha is a natural transformation; qed. Justified.

OVERALL: both directions are proved in both proofs, the interchange (f,g) = (id_{C'},g) o (f,id_D) is used correctly, and the componentwise hypotheses are instantiated at the right objects (C' rather than C where needed). The only defects are three typographical slips (0041/0080 label F where G is meant; 0181 f where g is meant; 0218 G where F is meant on the right-hand side); each is locally self-correcting, none is relied on in a corrupted form, and the logical skeleton is complete. Verdict VALID.
